newsitem.title: UK: British Labour government would be tragedy - Major.
newsitem.headline: British Labour government would be tragedy - Major.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major, unbowed by an opinion poll showing the Labour opposition holds a huge lead just weeks from an election, on Tuesday warned a change of political direction would be a "tragedy" for Britain.
In a BBC radio phone-in programme he gave his clearest hint that Britain will go to the polls on May 1 and said Britain's healthy economy would be jeopardised by a change of government.
"What is going right in this country can be seen right across the board," Major said. "It would be a great tragedy were we to change political direction and throw a lot of that away."

He said Labour lacked the political instincts which impelled Conservatives to keep inflation down and public spending under control and to rely on the private sector to run key industries and services.
Major's Conservatives, in power since 1979, had the support of just 30 percent of the electorate against 48 percent for Labour in the poll in the Guardian newspaper.

The poll was taken in the aftermath of last week's Wirral South by-election in which Labour won a previously safe Conservative seat by almost 8,000 votes, plunging the ruling party into a minority in the House of Commons.
It showed Labour's lead up by two percentage points since January, confirming the evidence from Wirral South that the buoyant economy is not boosting Conservative election prospects.
An optimistic Tony Blair, the Labour leader, told a party meeting on Tuesday: "Many long-standing Conservative supporters have become disillusioned."
The Conservatives have been riven by splits over Europe and by allegations of sleaze, and are considered out of touch and lacking ideas by many voters.
Major could still call an election for any Thursday between the end of March and May 22.
But asked by a questioner whether he planned to pick May 1, as widely reported, he said: "There is a fair expectation."
However, he added: "I think we will announce it (the date) in the normal constitutional way."
